channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: South African airline defends dramatic low-level flyby before rugby union clash
item.description: Cape Town stunt sparks major debate over safety risksAirlink insist flyby conducted according to regulationsA pre-game stunt involving two passenger jets flying dramatically low over a stadium in South Africa drew huge cheers from the estimated crowd of around 56,000 people, but also sparked a major debate over safety risks. South African airline defends dramatic low-level flyby before rugby union clash.

item.title: Morocco not to blame for Ceuta border breach, says Spanish PM
item.description: Pedro Sánchez says two countries are cooperating after mass incursion by 70,000 people into north African enclave Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has insisted there was no evidence to suggest the Moroccan government was behind last month’s massive border crossing into Ceuta. As many as 141 people are thought to have died trying to enter the Spanish enclave at the end of July.

item.title: Warm Yellow Sea strengthens storms in South Korea
item.description: More than 200mm of rain forecast in parts of South Korea, while parts of southern Europe to be 10C above averageSouth Korea’s prime minister, Han Seong-sook, met officials to prepare for heavy rain expected this week, with rainfall totals across central and northern parts of the country forecast to exceed 200mm in some areas. Warm Yellow Sea strengthens storms in South Korea.

item.title: China shows way in new pharma race: Own meds, don’t just make ’em
item.description: Pharmaceutical geopolitics is usually mapped through factories. China’s vast pharmaceutical supply chain, India’s strength in low-cost generics and the concentration of patented drug discovery in richer economies have shaped that discussion for years. But that map is becoming incomplete. Two developments in China this past week point to the next layer of competition. item.title: Minsk-Karachi railway shows Eurasia’s quiet geopolitical rewiring
item.description: The news that Pakistan, Russia, and Belarus are working on a test freight railway connecting Minsk, Moscow, and Karachi may seem like just another infrastructure project needing funding and construction. However, the real importance of this initiative lies in what it shows about the rapid shift in Eurasia’s economic geography. The project, revealed by Pakistan’s [] The post Minsk-Karachi railway.

item.title: US Conducts Fresh Strikes On Iran, Seen As 'Signal' To Tehran On Hormuz
item.description: US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz after the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) was observed preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines into the vital waterway, a US official confirmed to RFE/RL. US Strike On Iranian Launchers Signals Resolve To Keep Hormuz Open, Experts Say. US Conducts Fresh Strikes On Iranian Launchers, Seen As "Signal' To Tehran On Hormuz.

item.title: Ukrainian Officials Blamed For 'Negligence' After Deadly Strikes
item.description: With at least 38 people killed in Russian air attacks on the Kyiv region, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said "terrible negligence" was a factor in the high death toll. Ukrainian authorities have pledged to investigate why a weapons storage depot was located close to a populated area. Ukrainian Officials Blamed for 'Negligence' After Deadly Strikes.

item.title: ‘The lake is our life’: Protecting a shared lifeline in Uganda
item.description: On the shores of Nkondo, in Uganda’s Kikuube district, the day begins before sunrise. Fishers enter the lake to fish, while families around Lake Albert rely on its waters for food, income and daily survival. ‘The lake is our life’: Protecting a shared lifeline in Uganda.

item.title: Bangladesh’s J-10CE fighter plan stirs China dependence fears
item.description: Bangladesh’s planned J-10CE purchase could significantly strengthen its airpower while tying that capability more closely to Chinese weapons, support networks and supply chains. This month, multiple media outlets reported that Bangladesh is moving toward one of its largest defense procurements in years, preparing to buy Chinese J-10CE fighter jets as part of an air force [] The post Bangladesh’s Bangladesh’s J-10CE fighter plan stirs China dependence fears.

item.title: Zelenskyy Blasts 'Negligence' As Ukraine Mourns Dozens Killed In Russian Strike
item.description: Ukrainian rescue crews early on August 30 continued to search for victims of the deadly Russian attack outside of Kyiv, while local residents -- as well as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy -- demanded answers as to why explosives were stored in a warehouse so near private housing. Zelenskyy Blasts 'Negligence' As Ukraine Mourns Dozens Killed In Russian Strike.

item.title: Was it a mistake for 99 Colombian guerrillas to lay down their arms?
item.description: ‘Total peace’ plan of previous government led only 99 of Colombia’s 30,000 armed combatants to disarm, but new president Abelardo De la Espriella opposes peace agreementsIn mid-June, 99 guerrilla fighters were flown by helicopter to a small settlement in a rural area of southern Colombia where they lined up and, one by one, handed their weapons to government officials: rifles, pistols, machine gun.

item.description: Nepal reverses earlier decision and says foreign teams will be allowed to help with rescue efforts‘The flood took everything I have’: survivors grieve for relatives and homes swept away in NepalVisual guide: how the deadly flooding unfoldedTell us: have you been affected by the flash floods? Number of missing rises to 2,478; bodies recovered down rivers in India – latest updates.

item.description: Critics call move to gain long-term access to country’s massive energy reserves ‘predatory’ and ‘unconstitutional’Reports that the US is preparing to claim a big stake in Venezuela’s massive energy reserves have sparked an outcry, with critics describing the move as “predatory” and a “rapacious” land grab. item.title: Egyptian queen’s 673-diamond necklace stolen in Vienna smash-and-grab raid
item.description: Police hunt two suspects after historic 200-carat piece is snatched from Austrian museum during opening hoursAustrian police are hunting two men alleged to have stolen a 200-carat platinum necklace encrusted with 673 diamonds that was on loan to a museum in Vienna and once belonged to Egyptian royalty. Egyptian queen’s 673-diamond necklace stolen in Vienna smash-and-grab raid.

item.title: Civilian risks grow as military activity continues, UN says
item.description: Damaged roads, disrupted services and ongoing military activity continue to put civilians at risk in south Lebanon as strikes between Israeli forces and Hezbollah continue, according to the UN’s peacekeeping mission in the country (UNIFIL). UN warns of growing civilian risks as military activity continues. Civilian risks grow as military activity continues, UN says.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Tracking Syria’s transition
item.description: As Damascus continues to rebuild after more than a decade of war – from the recent dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces to the United States’ removal of Syria from its sponsors of terrorism list – a top UN official warned the Security Council on Thursday that international support can help tackle outstanding challenges. UN News app users can follow here.

item.title: Shock and devastation remain, a day after Himalayan flood disaster
item.description: Amid reports that hundreds of people are still missing in Nepal and China after a floodwater surge slammed into towns and villages on Wednesday, aid teams have been working to reach communities cut off by the disaster. Shock and devastation remain, a day after Himalayan flood disaster.

item.title: Hollow Promises: Resetting Gaza’s Ceasefire
item.description: A July roadmap sponsored by the Board of Peace has failed to overcome obstacles that have mired Gaza’s ceasefire deal ten months on. A mix of sustained pressure and diplomatic guarantees is needed to break the logjam and centre Palestinian agency in the strip's recovery. Hollow Promises: Resetting Gaza’s Ceasefire.

item.title: Curbing Reprisals in Syria
item.description: Fuelled by wartime grievances, mob attacks and other forms of retribution threaten Syria’s transition. Damascus has done too little to deter such acts. It should ensure visible legal consequences for violence and broaden locally rooted policing to rebuild trust among vulnerable communities. Curbing Reprisals in Syria.
